problem:
A numerical method is used to approximate a solution to an initial value problem, resulting in the table below. If the exact solution is $y(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ find, rounded to three decimal places, the global truncation error at each step.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.1$ | $0.099$ | {{field-1}} |
| $2$ | $0.3$ | $0.285$ | {{field-2}} |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.540$ | {{field-3}} |

feedback.problem:
A numerical method is used to approximate a solution to an initial value problem, resulting in the table below. If the exact solution is $y(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x),$ find, rounded to three decimal places, the global truncation error at each step.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.000$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.2$ | $0.920$ | {{field-1}} |
| $2$ | $0.4$ | $0.620$ | {{field-2}} |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.240$ | {{field-3}} |
feedback.worked_solution:
The global truncation error (GTE) is the total error accumulated after several steps of a numerical method. The GTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from ${x}_{n-1}$ to ${x}_{n}={x}_{n-1}+Δx$ is

$$
{e}_{n}=y({x}_{n})-{y}_{n},
$$

where $y({x}_{n})$ is the exact value at ${x}_{n},$ and ${y}_{n}$ is the numerical value produced after $n$ steps.

We are given the numerical values ${y}_{n}$ produced at each step in the table. Now, we compute the exact value $y({x}_{n})$ at each value of ${x}_{n}:$

- The exact value at ${x}_{0}=0$ is $y(0)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1.$

- The exact value at ${x}_{1}=0.2$ is $y(0.2)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.2).$

- The exact value at ${x}_{2}=0.4$ is $y(0.4)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.4).$

- The exact value at ${x}_{3}=0.6$ is $y(0.6)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.6).$

Let's add these values to the table.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | $y({x}_{n})$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.000$ | $1$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.2$ | $0.920$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.2)$ |  |
| $2$ | $0.4$ | $0.620$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.4)$ |  |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.240$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.6)$ |  |

Finally, we find the GTE at each step, rounding to three decimal places in each case:

- The GTE of the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{1} & =y({x}_{1})-{y}_{1} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.2)-0.920 \\  & ≈0.001.\end{aligned}
$$

- The GTE of the second step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{2} & =y({x}_{2})-{y}_{2} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.4)-0.620 \\  & ≈0.077.\end{aligned}
$$

- The GTE of the third step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{3} & =y({x}_{3})-{y}_{3} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.6)-0.240 \\  & ≈0.122.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | $y({x}_{n})$ | ${e}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.000$ | $1$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.2$ | $0.920$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.2)$ | $0.001$ |
| $2$ | $0.4$ | $0.620$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.4)$ | $0.077$ |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.240$ | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0.6)$ | $0.122$ |
